A1.justification: Despite substantial retitling and refocusing, both PDFs describe WiserUI-Bench and retain matching examples, benchmark distributions, and human-study votes. Both versions, including all appendices, support reliable comparison; figures with extraction problems were inspected visually.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, computational-cost measurements, and a 55-participant human study in Table 1 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V3 reports original selection and rationale-alignment experiments, evaluator validation against human judgments, and model evaluations against human-study preferences in Tables 2–5 and the supplement.

M1.justification: V1's proposed G-FOCUS procedure—goal extraction, difference localization, contrastive reasoning, and rationale ranking—is removed, including its Section 4 specification and Appendix E prompts. V3 instead evaluates existing models and reasoning strategies without proposing a replacement prediction algorithm.

E1.justification: The 300-pair web/mobile benchmark and synthetic-UI human study remain. However, v3 introduces an independent task requiring models to explain a supplied, verified winner. V1 evaluated rationales generated during winner selection, with BERTScore restricted to cases having a correct selection in at least one order. This substantially changes the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: V3 removes evaluated LLaVA-CoT, Llama-3.2-90B-Vision, and UICrit comparisons and adds Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL-2.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and LLaVA-OneVision models. CoCoT, Self-Refine, DDCoT, and both MAD variants remain for GPT-4o and Claude. The human study replaces G-FOCUS versus MAD predictions with comparisons among four models; UICrit remains related work rather than an evaluated system.

E3.justification: Reported temperature changes from 1 to 0.2, and GPT-4o changes from gpt-4o-2024-11-20 to gpt-4o-2024-08-06; Claude's identifier also changes. V3 replaces the C/CA selection reporting with FA/SA/AA/CA and adds winner-conditioned, GPT-4o-judged rationale evaluation plus additional text metrics. V1's OmniParser and self-consistency setup is no longer documented. These are materially different reported protocols, without establishing how experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds rationale-accuracy analysis across perception, memory, and action, and validates its rationale evaluator on 1,000 human-judged samples. It replaces G-FOCUS consistency demonstrations with model-specific selection and explanation cases. V1's UI-difference t-SNE analysis disappears, while the existing comparison of reasoning strategies is retained and revised.

E5.justification: V1 reports three-sample self-consistency and token-count dispersion, but no comparable performance-variability tables. V3 explicitly reports averages over three independent runs and adds standard deviations for selection and synthetic-UI evaluations in Tables D and G. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; it does not establish an increase in run count.

E6.justification: G-FOCUS results disappear, while model-selection, rationale-alignment, and human-study prediction results are extensively replaced or added. For example, GPT-4o zero-shot CA changes from 24.67% in v1 Table 1 to 30.11% in v3 Table 2 under revised settings, so this is not a same-setting gain. V3 newly reports o1 rationale-wise accuracy of 64.18% and instance-wise accuracy of 78.33%. Human vote counts remain identical.

T1.justification: V1's elementary mathematical definitions of G-FOCUS goal sampling, localization, rationale generation, and evaluation disappear with the method. Its separately defined Consistency statistic is also dropped. CA retains its meaning in v3's prose, and neither version contains substantial theoretical derivations or proofs; the change is chiefly a limited loss of formal specification.

C1.justification: V1's central contribution includes a superior bias-mitigating inference method and its potential as a reliable preference verifier. V3 removes those claims and centers its contributions on a behavior-oriented benchmark, two independent assessment tasks, and evidence that current MLLMs have limited UI/UX reasoning. Behavior-aware generation remains a prospective application.

C2.justification: V1 interprets G-FOCUS's results as supporting scalable preference verification. V3 treats the human study as exploratory and adds interpretations concerning partial rationale coverage, model scaling, cognitive-dimension differences, and excessive debate. Its limitations discussion retains cultural and interactive-UI caveats but reframes dataset size around scarce public A/B results and removes method-specific applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents baseline and evaluator prompts, open-model checkpoints, four RTX A6000 GPUs, operating system, and library versions, while removing G-FOCUS prompts and t-SNE implementation details. Annotation documentation changes from revising GPT-4o drafts to collaborative expert writing with UX-law tags, without establishing whether every annotation was redone. Listed data sources also change, and a repository link and release statement replace v1's future-release promise.

R1.justification: V3 substantially repositions the work around behavior-grounded UI/UX understanding. It adds a comparison of existing UI evaluation benchmarks, Norman-based cognitive framing, and substantive discussion of human-behavior simulation, including Generative Agents, UXAgent, and AgentA/B. V1's emphasis on interactive visual prompting and VLM-as-a-Judge bias research is substantially reduced.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the benchmark. The method section becomes a task-description section, dedicated analyses are introduced, discussion and conclusion are combined, and limitations and ethics move into reorganized supplementary material. This exceeds terminology changes or added scientific content alone.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with substantially redesigned overview and curation figures. G-FOCUS diagrams disappear; task, rationale-distribution, and cognitive-dimension figures are added. Result tables are reorganized by task, and retained distribution plots are combined with a new change-type plot. Existing preprocessing and human-study screenshots are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's selection-conditioned BERTScore analysis, v3's separate explanation task and human-checked evaluator provide more informative evidence about reasoning. Performance variability and fuller implementation details also improve transparency. The net gain is limited by removal of the tested G-FOCUS solution, moderate evaluator agreement (kappa 0.42), and reporting weaknesses: for example, Section 3.2 gives landing pages as 18.3%, whereas Figure K retains 15.3%.
